title: The index is committed only where the committed shards support it
desiredOutcome: commit-manifest-index never records an index that names tasks or phases its committed shards do not hold - it refuses and names the shard to commit first - and the notes that point at it state the order

findings.resolution: fixed in P68.2-v4q: one git status, git show only for changed shards (cmi26)

review.outcome: matches; two findings (one med, one low) fixed in P68.2-v4q

summary: commit-manifest-index no longer records an index ahead of the shards it names: it refuses, before staging anything, an index naming a task or phase the shard committed at HEAD does not hold yet - a fileIndex entry, a bug's fix task, a new phase stub - naming each and the shard to commit first; a widened scope on a committed task and a dangling id still commit. The note audit-task prints states the order (the shard first), and the check asks git only about shards that changed, so its cost follows the change, not the plan. Fixes BUG-10, found signing off P66. This phase was run in that order - each task commit carried its shard, the index followed - and its invariant check found no breach. Reviewed in phase mode (two findings, fixed); the phase gate ran green with the tree unchanged.

tasks.title: Fix BUG-10: commit-manifest-index commits an index ahead of the shards it names
tasks.description: Repro: audit-task add on a sharded plan, then commit-manifest-index before the shard is committed; git show HEAD's index plus HEAD's shard fails validation (fileIndex names a task that does not exist). Expected: the index is committed only in a state the committed shards support, or the command names the shard to commit first. Actual: the index commit lands and the plan as that commit records it fails validation; audit-task's own note says to land it before or beside the next commit.
